# Boletus (grupo edulis) / Porcini (Boletus edulis group)

*Boletus edulis group (B. edulis, B. aereus, B. reticulatus, B. pinophilus)*

Ectomycorrhizal with beech, oaks, pines and others. The group spans species with different hosts and seasons (B. reticulatus and B. aereus fruit earlier, in warmer weather); one model covers them all, so treat it as coarse.

**Habitats:** beech, mixed, oak, pine

## Season

Ramps up from 07-15, peak 09-01 to 10-31, ends 11-30. Evidence grade **C**.

GBIF near Tierra Estella, n=46: Jun 1, Jul 4, Aug 2, Sep 15, Oct 20, Nov 3, Dec 1.

### Rationale

- **rain:** Rain over the 21 days ending 5 days before, approximating the 26-day window in which a decade of beech-forest monitoring found fruiting increasing linearly with precipitation (no upper threshold found). The curve's values are ours. (porcini_preprint2025, martinezpena2012)
- **temperature:** Peak fruiting was associated with a mean of about 13 °C over the previous 20 days (preprint, beech forests). The plateau and tails are ours. (porcini_preprint2025)
- **water_balance:** Water balance (rain minus evaporative demand) explained yields better than rain alone in Mediterranean pine stands. Values are ours. (agreda2015)
- **heat:** Sudden rises in maximum temperature appeared to inhibit porcini productivity. (salerni2023)
- **frost:** Frosts end the autumn flush; the counts are ours. (field_guides, boddy2014)

## References

- `agreda2015`: Ágreda, T., Águeda, B., Olano, J. M., Vicente-Serrano, S. M. & Fernández-Toirán, M. (2015). Increased evapotranspiration demand in a Mediterranean climate might cause a decline in fungal yields under global warming. Global Change Biology 21(9): 3499-3510. doi:10.1111/gcb.12960
- `boddy2014`: Boddy, L. et al. (2014). Climate variation effects on fungal fruiting. Fungal Ecology 10: 20-33.
- `field_guides`: Consensus of European field guides and regional mycological societies on habitat and season. Not a single source; grade C at best.
- `gbif_tierra_estella`: GBIF.org occurrence records in the box 42.4-43.0 N, 2.6-1.6 W (Tierra Estella, Urbasa and surroundings), monthly counts queried 2026-11-07. Finds only, with collection bias: used to check seasons, not thresholds.
- `martinezpena2012`: Martínez-Peña, F. et al. (2012). Yield models for ectomycorrhizal mushrooms in Pinus sylvestris forests with special focus on Boletus edulis and Lactarius group deliciosus. Forest Ecology and Management.
- `porcini_preprint2025`: Predicting porcini: a decade of sporocarp monitoring reveals the meteorological triggers of Boletus edulis fruiting in central European beech forests. bioRxiv preprint (2025), doi:10.64898/2025.12.12.693895. Not peer-reviewed.
- `salerni2023`: Salerni, E., Paoli, L. & Perini, C. (2023). Italian Journal of Mycology: three years of porcini productivity in Abies alba plantations in relation to extreme rain and temperature events and thinning. https://italianmycology.unibo.it/article/view/16464
